from math import gcd


def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    # Current candidate average p/q, starting from the whole array.
    p = sum(a)
    q = n
    while True:
        # Prefix sums of (q*a_i - p) decide whether any subarray beats p/q.
        # Also track plain prefix sums of a to recover the subarray's sum.
        pre_val = [0] * (n + 1)
        pre_sum = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i, x in enumerate(a):
            pre_val[i + 1] = pre_val[i] + (q * x - p)
            pre_sum[i + 1] = pre_sum[i] + x

        # Find the subarray (i, j] of length >= k maximizing sum(q*a - p).
        best = 0
        best_pair = None
        min_idx = 0
        for j in range(k, n + 1):
            i = j - k
            if pre_val[i] < pre_val[min_idx]:
                min_idx = i
            cand = pre_val[j] - pre_val[min_idx]
            if cand > best:
                best = cand
                best_pair = (min_idx, j)

        # No subarray has average strictly above p/q: it is the optimum.
        if best_pair is None:
            break

        # Move to the better average. It is strictly larger, so this terminates.
        i, j = best_pair
        p = pre_sum[j] - pre_sum[i]
        q = j - i

    g = gcd(p, q)
    return [p // g, q // g]
